**Accounted4Tax Ltd** · Registered office: 128 City Road, London EC1V 2NX · Company no. 16438537 · info@accounted4tax.co.uk · work carried out under our director's AAT practising licence (AAT membership no. 10424835)

{{letter_date}} · Quote ref {{quote_number}}

{{client_name}} {{business_name}} {{client_address}}

Dear {{client_first_name}},

**Engagement letter**

Thank you for choosing Accounted4Tax Ltd. Your work will be done and overseen by our AAT-licensed accountant, who will be your main contact. This letter, your quote {{quote_number}}, the attached schedule(s) of services, our standard terms and conditions and our privacy notice set out the basis on which we will act. Together they form our contract.

**Who we are acting for**

`[IF individual]` We are acting for you, {{client_name}}, only. If you would like us to act for anyone else, such as your spouse, partner or a company, we will issue them a separate engagement letter.

`[IF ltd]` We are acting for {{company_name}} (company number {{company_number}}) only, and not for its directors or shareholders personally. {{nominated_person}} has agreed to act as the nominated director. By accepting this letter you confirm that the nominated director is authorised to give us instructions and information for the company and to receive our advice and work. Any change of nominated director must be notified to us in writing and takes effect only when we acknowledge it in writing.

We will ask HMRC to authorise us as your agent through our HMRC Agent Services Account. We will email you a link and simple instructions. Please complete the steps within the time HMRC allows, usually 30 days. If online authorisation does not work for Self Assessment, Corporation Tax or PAYE, we will send you a pre-filled form 64-8 to sign instead. You remain responsible for taking reasonable care over your tax affairs.

**Period of engagement**

This engagement starts on {{start_date}}. The first period we are responsible for is {{first_period}}. We will not deal with earlier periods unless you ask us to and we agree in writing.

The terms take effect when you accept this letter online. If you instruct us to start work before accepting, that instruction will be treated as acceptance of these terms unless you tell us otherwise within 14 days.

For ongoing services, this engagement runs to {{year_end}} and then renews each year on the same terms, unless either of us gives notice (terms, clause 20) or we agree new fees or services with you.

**Scope of services**

You have instructed us to carry out the following work:

{{services_list}}

The attached schedule(s) describe what each service includes, what it does not include, and what you and we are each responsible for. Only the services listed in the schedules are included. If you want us to do anything else, please ask and we will confirm the scope and fee in writing first.

**Fees**

Your fees, the payment option you chose and your payment dates are set out in your quote {{quote_number}}, attached as a PDF. The quote forms part of this agreement.

We are not registered for VAT, so no VAT is added to our fees.

- Fees are fixed for the work described, based on the information you gave us when we quoted (for example, the number of transactions, employees or subcontractors). If that information turns out to be materially different, we will tell you and agree any change before charging more.
- Work outside the schedules is charged at £50 per hour, or at a fixed fee we agree with you before starting.

Stripe will email you a numbered invoice or receipt for every payment. You can update your card, download invoices or cancel your subscription through the secure customer portal link in your welcome email. Cancelling your subscription does not by itself end this engagement; please also give us notice as set out in clause 20 of our terms.

**Before we can start: identity checks**

Our work is carried out under our director's AAT practising licence, and we are supervised by AAT under the Money Laundering Regulations 2017. We must verify your identity `[IF ltd]` and that of the company's directors and beneficial owners `[END]` before we start any work. After you accept, we will email you a secure link to upload photo ID and proof of address. **We cannot start work until these checks are complete.**

**Limitation of liability**

**Please read clause 18 of our standard terms and the final paragraph of each schedule. They set out how we limit our liability to you. Clause 19 excludes liability to third parties. No third party may rely on our work under this letter.**

**Data protection**

We take your privacy seriously. We will only use your personal information, and information you give us about others, to provide the services you have asked for, to run your account and to meet our legal duties. Our privacy notice (attached) explains how. Please note:

- `[IF alternate]` **Alternate arrangements.** If our principal accountant is permanently unable to act through illness or incapacity, an alternate practitioner will have access to your records so they can contact you and agree how your work continues. You may then appoint another adviser if you prefer. `[END]`
- **How we communicate.** We will use email, our secure online portal and quote pages, cloud accounting software (such as Xero, QuickBooks, FreeAgent or Sage), and post where needed. Ordinary email is not encrypted; by accepting, you accept that risk. Tell us if you want a more secure method for any document.

`[IF consumer]`

**Your right to cancel**

You have the right to cancel this contract within 14 days without giving any reason. The 14 days start on the day you accept this letter online.

To cancel, tell us clearly before the 14 days end, for example by emailing info@accounted4tax.co.uk. You may use the cancellation form in Part E, but you do not have to.

If you cancel, we will refund all payments you have made within 14 days of being told, using the same payment method, at no cost to you. **If you asked us to start work during the 14 days, we will deduct an amount in proportion to the work we have done up to the time you told us you were cancelling.**

`[END consumer]`

**Your agreement**

Please read this letter, the schedule(s), the standard terms and the privacy notice, then accept them on the next screen. Your typed name, the date and time, and your device details will be recorded as your signature.

Yours sincerely,

For and on behalf of Accounted4Tax Ltd

**Attached:** Quote {{quote_number}} (PDF) · {{schedules_list}} · Standard terms and conditions of business · Privacy notice `[IF consumer]` · Cancellation form `[END]`

Accounted4Tax Ltd · Version 1.0, 11 November 2026. Read these terms with the engagement letter, the schedules and the privacy notice. "We", "us" and "our" mean Accounted4Tax Ltd. "You" means the client named in the engagement letter.

**1. Applicable law.** These terms, the engagement letter and the schedules are governed by the law of England and Wales, and the courts of England and Wales have exclusive jurisdiction over any dispute. If you are a consumer living in Scotland or Northern Ireland, you may also bring proceedings in your local courts.

**2. Identity checks.** We must identify and verify our clients under UK anti-money laundering law. Save in exceptional circumstances we cannot start work until this is done. We may ask for, and keep, documents and information for this purpose, and may use electronic ID verification. We must also keep this information up to date, so we may ask again during the engagement. You must tell us if your business needs its own anti-money laundering supervision, for example if you make or accept cash payments of €10,000 or more for goods.

**3. Anti-money laundering reporting.** We must comply with the Proceeds of Crime Act 2002, the Terrorism Act 2000 and the Money Laundering Regulations 2017. If we know or suspect, or have reasonable grounds to suspect, that you or anyone connected with you is involved in money laundering (which includes the proceeds of tax evasion), we must report it to the National Crime Agency. We may not tell you we have done so, and we may have to stop work until we are permitted to continue. We are not liable for any loss caused by our compliance with these duties.

**4. Client money.** We do not hold client money. Fees are paid to us by card through Stripe. Tax refunds will be paid by HMRC directly to you, not to us.

**5. Commissions.** If we receive any commission or benefit for introducing you to another business, we will tell you in writing the amount and terms.

**6. Complaints.** We aim to give you a high-quality service. If you are unhappy with any part of it, please email us at info@accounted4tax.co.uk. We will acknowledge your complaint within 5 working days, investigate it carefully and reply in full within 30 days. If you are still not satisfied, you can complain to our professional body, AAT (Association of Accounting Technicians), at aat.org.uk/complaints.

**7. Confidentiality.** Communications between us are confidential. We will take all reasonable steps not to disclose your information except where the law, a regulator, our insurers or our professional body requires it, or as set out in the privacy notice. This continues after the engagement ends. If we subcontract work to another qualified accountant, they will be bound by the same confidentiality and security terms.

**8. Conflicts of interest.** If we identify a conflict of interest that can be managed with suitable safeguards, we will apply them, with your informed consent where possible. If it cannot be managed, we will tell you promptly and may have to stop acting. We may act for other clients whose interests differ from yours, subject always to confidentiality.

**9. Data protection.** We will process your personal data in line with UK GDPR, the Data Protection Act 2018 and our privacy notice. Where we act as a data processor for you (for example in payroll), the data-processing annex to that schedule also applies.

**10. Electronic communication.** We will communicate with you by email, through our online systems and through cloud accounting software. Electronic communication carries risks of non-receipt, delay, misdirection, interception and viruses. We use reasonable security, but we are not liable for loss caused by these risks unless caused by our negligence. Please tell us if you prefer paper, except where online filing is compulsory. Letters we post are treated as received two working days after posting. When we access your HMRC online records, we will only look at what we reasonably need. Please keep your contact details up to date with us.

**11. Fees and payment.**

- Our fees are fixed fees for the work described in the schedules, based on the information you gave us. If the work turns out to be materially different (for example more transactions, employees or subcontractors, or poor records), we will tell you and agree a revised fee before doing the extra work.
- Fixed fees are set for one year at a time. We will tell you of any change at least 30 days before your renewal date.
- One-off fees are paid in full by card when you accept. Monthly fees are taken by card on the same date each month through Stripe and end after the last payment due before your year end.
- If a payment fails, Stripe will retry it. If it remains unpaid for 14 days, we may pause work (including submissions) after telling you in writing, and we will not be liable for penalties caused by that pause. We will only do this where it is fair and reasonable.
- `[IF business client]` We may charge interest on late payments at 8% above the Bank of England base rate under the Late Payment of Commercial Debts (Interest) Act 1998.
- Our fees do not include third-party costs, such as Companies House or HMRC fees, or software subscriptions, unless the schedule says so.
- If you think an invoice is wrong, please tell us within 21 days of receiving it.
- If you have fee protection insurance or similar cover, tell us. You remain liable for our fees whether or not your insurer pays.
- If you move to another accountant, we may charge a reasonable fee for preparing handover information beyond the standard professional clearance letter.

**12. Implementation of advice.** We will only help you put our advice into practice if you ask us to and we agree in writing.

**13. Intellectual property.** We keep copyright in all documents we prepare, except where the law says otherwise. You may use them for the purpose they were prepared for.

**14. Interpretation.** If any part of these terms is found invalid, the rest still applies. If these terms conflict with the engagement letter or a schedule, the letter or schedule takes precedence.

**15. Disputes within a business client.** Where our client is a company, we will not give information or services to one director or shareholder without the knowledge of the others. If we receive conflicting instructions from different directors, we will refer the matter to the board and take no further action until it decides.

**16. Investment advice.** We are not authorised by the Financial Conduct Authority to give investment, pension or insurance advice. If you need such advice we may refer you to someone who is.

**17. Lien.** As far as the law and our professional rules allow, we may keep documents and records belonging to you until all fees due are paid. This never applies to records you need to meet a statutory deadline.

**18. Limitation of liability.**

- We will provide our services with reasonable care and skill. We are liable only for losses, damages, costs and expenses directly caused by our negligence, fraud or wilful default.
- *Loss caused by others.* We are not liable for losses, penalties, interest or extra tax caused by the acts or omissions of anyone else, by incomplete, misleading or false information given to us, or by a failure to act on our advice or to give us relevant information. Where we refer you to another firm that you engage directly, we are not responsible for its work.
- *Circumstances beyond our control.* We are not liable for delay or failure caused by circumstances outside our reasonable control, including HMRC or Companies House system failures.
- *Non-disclosure or misrepresentation.* We are not liable for loss caused by information being withheld, concealed or misrepresented to us, unless it should reasonably have been evident to us in doing the agreed work with reasonable care and skill.
- *Unauthorised disclosure.* You agree to indemnify us against any claim arising from your unauthorised disclosure of our advice to others, including our reasonable costs of defending it.
- *Aggregate cap.* Our total liability to you, and to anyone else entitled to rely on our work, for all claims connected with this engagement is limited to the total fees you paid us under this engagement in the 12 months before the event giving rise to the claim. By accepting the engagement letter you agree this limit is reasonable. If you do not, please contact us before accepting.
- Nothing in these terms limits liability for death or personal injury caused by negligence, for fraud, or any other liability that cannot be limited by law, including your statutory rights as a consumer.

**19. Third parties.** Our advice and work are for your sole use. We accept no responsibility to anyone else, including group companies, directors personally, lenders or landlords, unless we have agreed so in writing. No one else has rights under the Contracts (Rights of Third Parties) Act 1999.

**20. Period of engagement and termination.**

- Our work begins when you accept the engagement letter (or instruct us to start). We are not responsible for periods before the first period stated in the letter.
- Either of us may end the engagement by giving at least 21 days' notice in writing (email is fine). We may end it immediately if you do not cooperate with us, if we believe you have given us or HMRC misleading information, or if the law or our professional rules require it.
- When the engagement ends we will try to agree how to complete work in progress. We owe no further duties after the termination date. Fees for work done up to that date remain payable. Where you pay monthly, any balance owed for work already completed will be invoiced, and any amount paid for work not yet started will be refunded.
- For one-off work (for example a single tax return or a registration), the engagement ends when that work is completed.
- If we have had no contact from you for 12 months, we may send a disengagement letter to your last known address and stop acting.
- We will normally confirm the end of an engagement with a disengagement letter (Part F) and tell HMRC we no longer act for you.

**21. Professional rules.** We follow the bye-laws, regulations and ethical code of AAT and the guidance *Professional Conduct in Relation to Taxation* (PCRT), available at aat.org.uk. We will not take part in tax planning that breaches PCRT, the general anti-abuse rule or targeted anti-avoidance rules. You authorise us to correct errors made by HMRC that we become aware of. If you become aware of an error in a return after it has been filed, tell us so we can help you correct it. If you refuse to correct an error or tell HMRC about it, we may have to stop acting and tell HMRC we no longer act for you, and we may have to make a report as in clause 3.

**22. Reliance on advice.** We record important advice in writing. Oral advice should not be relied on unless we confirm it in writing. Advice is valid only at the date given and on the facts you gave us.

**23. Records.** You are legally responsible for keeping your records. By law they must be kept for at least: individuals with trading or rental income, 5 years after the 31 January filing deadline (5 years 10 months after the tax year ends); other individuals, 22 months after the tax year ends; companies, 6 years from the end of the accounting period. We will return original documents on request. We keep our files for 7 years after the engagement ends and then securely destroy them. When we stop acting, we will help you take over access to any cloud accounting software; you may then need to pay the software provider directly.

**24. Professional indemnity insurance.** As AAT requires, we hold professional indemnity insurance. Our insurer is AXA Insurance. Details of the cover, including its territorial coverage, are available on request.

**25. Changes to these terms.** If we need to change these terms, we will email you the new version at least 30 days before it takes effect. Work you instruct after that date is carried out on the new terms. Significant changes to scope or fees will need your agreement.

**Who we are.** Accounted4Tax Ltd (company 16438537), 128 City Road, London EC1V 2NX, is the data controller for your personal data. We are registered with the Information Commissioner's Office, registration number ZC296363. Contact for data protection: info@accounted4tax.co.uk. We are not required to appoint a Data Protection Officer.

**What we collect and where from.** Names, contact details, date of birth, National Insurance number, UTR and other tax references, identity documents and proof of address, bank statements and financial records, income and tax details, and (for payroll or CIS) details of your employees or subcontractors. We get this from you, from HMRC, from Companies House, from your bank feeds and accounting software (with your permission), from electronic ID verification providers, and from your previous accountant.

**Why we use it and our legal basis**

| Purpose | Legal basis (UK GDPR Article 6) |
|---|---|
| Preparing your quote and engagement letter | Steps before a contract, at your request |
| Providing the services you have asked for | Contract |
| Identity checks and anti-money laundering duties | Legal obligation (Money Laundering Regulations 2017) |
| Meeting tax, company and professional body requirements (AAT) | Legal obligation |
| Taking payment and managing fees, including disputes | Contract and legitimate interests |
| Defending complaints, disciplinary or legal claims | Legitimate interests |
| Emailing you about our other services | Consent (you can withdraw it at any time) |

If you do not give us the information we need, we may not be able to act for you.

**Who we share it with.** HMRC; Companies House; The Pensions Regulator and pension providers (payroll clients); AAT and the Office for Professional Body Anti-Money Laundering Supervision (OPBAS) for supervision and quality checks; our professional indemnity insurers and their advisers; [IF alternate] our alternate practitioner if our principal accountant cannot act; [END] subcontractors bound by confidentiality; anyone you ask us to deal with; and, where the law requires, the National Crime Agency, police, courts and the ICO. We never sell your data.

**Systems we use.** Your data is held in secure cloud services that are bound by data protection terms: our quote and client database (with ID documents in private, encrypted storage), our card payment provider, our email delivery service, our email and file storage services, and cloud accounting and tax software. Ask us if you would like the names of the providers.

**Transfers outside the UK.** Some of these providers store or access data outside the UK, including in the EU and the USA. Where they do, we rely on UK adequacy regulations (for example the EU, and the UK Extension to the EU–US Data Privacy Framework) or the UK International Data Transfer Agreement or Addendum, so your data has equivalent protection. Ask us for details.

**How long we keep it.** For 7 years after the end of the tax year or accounting period the work relates to, or 7 years after our relationship ends if later. Identity (anti-money laundering) records are kept for 5 years after the relationship ends, as the law requires. Information needed for more than one year (for example capital gains base costs or elections) is kept throughout our relationship and then for 7 years. After that we delete it securely. Keep your own copies of the returns and documents we send you.

**Payroll.** When we run payroll for you, you are the controller of your employees' data and we act as your processor under the data-processing annex to Schedule D7.

**Your rights.** You can ask us to: give you a copy of your data (we reply within one month, normally free); correct it; delete it; restrict or object to our use of it; give it to you or another adviser in a portable format; or stop using it for marketing. Some rights are limited where we must keep data by law. Contact info@accounted4tax.co.uk. To protect you, we may need to check your identity first.

**Automated decisions.** We do not make decisions about you by automated means only. Our quote system calculates fees automatically, but every quote is reviewed and sent by us.

**Complaints.** If you are unhappy with how we handle your data, please tell us first. You can also complain to the ICO at ico.org.uk or on 0303 123 1113.

**Changes.** We will tell you of any significant change to this notice, including any new purpose or legal basis.

Typical examples are HMRC enquiries or compliance checks, amending earlier returns, penalty appeals, advice on one-off transactions, and phone or email queries beyond routine contact. We will tell you before doing extra work and agree the fee first where possible. Where specialist advice is needed, we may refer you to a specialist, but only with your instruction.

D1.title: Self Assessment tax return (individuals, sole traders, CIS subcontractors and landlords)
D1.body:
**We will:**

1. Prepare your Self Assessment tax return (SA100) and the supplementary pages needed (for example self-employment SA103, UK property SA105, employment SA102, capital gains SA108 for straightforward disposals) for {{first_period}}, from the records and information you give us.
2. Prepare a summary of your self-employment and/or property income and expenses (an income and expenditure statement) in line with HMRC rules, using cash basis or accruals basis as appropriate. This is not an audit.
3. Claim CIS deductions suffered, and capital allowances, losses and other reliefs that the information shows you are entitled to.
4. Calculate your income tax, Class 4 National Insurance and any capital gains tax, tell you how much to pay and when (including payments on account), and check HMRC's calculation.
5. Send you the return for approval and submit it online to HMRC once you approve it.
6. Tell you about the interest and penalties for late filing or payment.

**Fee basis:** the fee in your quote covers one tax return for the year stated. For the self-employed it is a base fee plus a charge for each £10,000 (or part of £10,000) of the estimated income you gave us; if your actual income is higher, we will tell you the final fee before charging it. The base fee is payable when you accept. The balance is taken from the card you saved with us before we submit your return to HMRC. Returns for earlier years are quoted as separate one-off fees.

**You agree to:**

- Give us full details of **all** your income, gains and claims, including income from abroad, by 31 October after the end of the tax year (or 10 working days before any earlier deadline). If information arrives later, we will try to meet the 31 January deadline but cannot guarantee it, and may charge for urgent work.
- Tell us within 60 days of completion about any sale of UK residential property, because a separate capital gains tax return and payment are due within 60 days. This is outside this schedule unless agreed.
- Check the return carefully before approving it. **You are legally responsible for the return being correct and complete, filing it by the deadline and paying tax on time. This cannot be delegated.**
- Keep proper records (receipts, invoices, bank statements, mileage logs) for the time the law requires.
- Keep an eye on your turnover and tell us if it may go over the VAT registration threshold (currently £90,000 in any rolling 12 months), and tell us if your qualifying income may bring you into Making Tax Digital for Income Tax.
- Tell us about changes in your circumstances, such as starting or stopping a business, marriage, or child benefit claims (High Income Child Benefit Charge).

D2.title: Making Tax Digital for Income Tax (MTD for IT)
D2.body:
**We will:**

1. `[All plans]` Register you for MTD for Income Tax through our Agent Services Account, once you have signed the authority below.
2. `[All plans]` Provide MTD-compatible accounting software, set it up, connect it to HMRC, hold an onboarding call with you and send you a reminder before each quarterly deadline. Support by email.
3. `[Essential]` You keep your own records and submit your own quarterly updates and final declaration; we do not review them. If you ask us to, we will prepare a quarterly update (£79 each) or your final declaration (from £99) as extra work.
4. `[Compliance / Full MTD]` Keep your books: categorise your transactions and reconcile your bank accounts (Schedule D3), up to 50 transactions a month on Compliance and up to 100 a month on Full MTD. Extra transactions are charged at £0.50 each.
5. `[Compliance / Full MTD]` Prepare and submit each quarterly update after you approve it (or, if you agree in writing, on the basis of the data you have given us). Quarterly updates are due by 7 August, 7 November, 7 February and 7 May.
6. `[Compliance / Full MTD]` Prepare and submit your final declaration (year-end return) by 31 January, as in Schedule D1, and give you a quarterly estimate of the tax to put aside. Support by email, phone and WhatsApp.
7. `[Full MTD]` Prepare and submit your VAT returns if you are VAT registered (Schedule D8). Priority support.
8. Each extra income source (another business or a property business) adds £20 a month to your plan.
9. Tell you if you may be exempt from MTD; applying for an exemption is extra work.

**You agree to:**

- Record income and expenses digitally in MTD-compatible software, or give us your full records, within 10 days after each quarter ends (quarters end 5 July, 5 October, 5 January, 5 April). We need at least 7 days before each deadline.
- Confirm that the records are complete and accurate before each submission.
- Understand that HMRC charges late submission penalty points for each missed update, and a financial penalty once the threshold is reached. If records are late we are not responsible for points or penalties.
- Understand that the software we provide is included in your fee while you use our MTD service. If you use your own software, you pay for it.

**Your monthly plan.** Your MTD plan has no end date: we collect the monthly fee by card each month until you cancel. To cancel, tell us in writing at least 14 days before your next monthly payment date; the plan then ends at the end of the period you have already paid for. Payments already made are not refunded.

**Authority to sign up for MTD for Income Tax (if sign-up is included).** By accepting, you instruct Accounted4Tax Ltd to sign you up for MTD for Income Tax and to send your personal and tax information to HMRC for that purpose. You confirm the information you gave us is accurate. You understand that once signed up, you must follow the MTD rules, and that you generally cannot leave simply by choice: you can only leave if you stop meeting the conditions or HMRC agrees.

D3.title: Bookkeeping
D3.body:
**We will:**

1. Record your business transactions in the accounting software we agree with you, monthly from your bank feeds, sales and purchase invoices, receipts and the explanations you give us.
2. Reconcile your bank and card accounts to the statements, and keep the records in line with generally accepted bookkeeping practice.
3. Ask you about transactions we cannot identify, and post unexplained items to a suspense account until you reply.
4. `[IF included]` Send you a short monthly profit and loss summary.

**Fee basis:** your fee is £30 a month for each batch of up to 50 transactions a month, as shown in your quote (one bank or card line = one transaction). If your volume moves into a higher batch for two months in a row, we will tell you and agree the new monthly fee before applying it.

**Not included:** payroll, VAT returns, CIS returns, management accounts, credit control, paying your suppliers, and clearing old backlogs (quoted separately as catch-up work).

**You agree to:** give us access to your bank feeds and software; upload receipts and invoices within 10 days of the period end; answer our queries promptly; and keep genuine, complete records. You are responsible for preventing and detecting fraud and errors in your business. We cannot guarantee to find them, but we will tell you about any we notice.

D4.title: CIS returns (contractors)
D4.body:
**We will:**

1. Verify new subcontractors with HMRC before you pay them, using the details you give us.
2. Calculate the CIS deduction for each payment you tell us about, at the rate HMRC gives.
3. Prepare your monthly CIS return (CIS300), including a nil return where needed, and submit it to HMRC by the 19th of the month after each tax month (tax months end on the 5th).
4. Prepare payment and deduction statements for you to give to each subcontractor by the 19th.
5. Tell you how much CIS to pay HMRC and by when (22nd of the month if paid electronically).

**Fee basis:** your fee covers the number of subcontractors in your quote. If the number rises above that, we will tell you and agree the new fee.

**You agree to:** send us the details of every payment to subcontractors (name, UTR, amount, cost of materials) and any new subcontractor's details at least 3 working days before the 19th; tell us if no payments were made; pay HMRC on time; and keep records for at least 3 years after the tax year. **As the contractor you are legally responsible for the returns, deductions and payments, and for deciding whether each worker is self-employed or an employee.** Late returns attract automatic penalties from HMRC, which we are not responsible for if information was late.

*CIS subcontractors who want to reclaim deductions do so through their Self Assessment return (Schedule D1), or a Ltd company's payroll (Schedule D7).*

D5.title: Limited company annual accounts and Corporation Tax return (including dormant companies)
D5.body:
**We will:**

1. Prepare the company's annual statutory accounts for the accounting period ending {{year_end}} from the records and information the directors give us, in line with the Companies Act 2006 and the applicable accounting standard (normally FRS 105 micro-entity or FRS 102 Section 1A small company).
2. Compile the accounts without carrying out an audit, and attach our accountant's report saying so. If we find the accounts do not follow accepted accounting principles, we will say so.
3. Prepare the Corporation Tax computation and Company Tax Return (CT600), apply the iXBRL tags required for online filing, and claim the allowances and reliefs the information supports.
4. Tell the directors how much Corporation Tax is due and when (normally 9 months and 1 day after the year end), and whether quarterly instalment payments apply.
5. Send the accounts and return for approval. Once a director approves them, file the accounts with Companies House (due 9 months after the year end) and the CT600 and accounts with HMRC (due 12 months after the year end).
6. Tell the directors about tax on loans to directors or shareholders (s455) shown in the records.
7. `[IF dormant]` For a dormant company, prepare and file dormant company accounts, and tell HMRC the company is dormant or file a nil CT600 if HMRC has issued a notice to deliver a return.

**Fee basis:** our fee for the accounts and Corporation Tax return starts from £349 a year and is set in your quote according to the size and complexity of the company. Bookkeeping is charged separately by the number of transactions (Schedule D3). Each earlier year whose accounts are still outstanding is quoted as a separate one-off fee.

**Not included:** bookkeeping (Schedule D3), payroll, VAT, the directors' personal tax returns (these need a separate engagement letter), audits, and advice on dividends, remuneration or transactions unless agreed.

**The directors agree to:**

- Keep adequate accounting records as the Companies Act requires, and give us all records, bank statements and year-end information (stock, debtors, creditors, loans, assets bought or sold) within 3 months after the year end.
- Tell us about all loans or payments to directors, shareholders or their families during the period.
- Review and approve the accounts and return. **The directors are legally responsible for the accounts giving a true and fair view, for the return being correct and complete, for filing on time and for paying tax on time. This cannot be delegated.**
- Safeguard the company's assets and take reasonable steps to prevent and detect fraud and other irregularities.
- Monitor turnover against the VAT registration threshold (currently £90,000 in any rolling 12 months) and tell us promptly if it may be exceeded.
- If the accounts are not prepared by us, provide approved accounts in iXBRL format and accept responsibility for their tagging.

D6.title: Company secretarial: confirmation statement and director identity verification
D6.body:
**We will:**

1. Review the company's details on the Companies House register (registered office, officers, people with significant control (PSCs), share capital, shareholders and SIC codes) with you before each review date.
2. Prepare and file the confirmation statement (CS01) within 14 days after the review date, including the statement that the company's intended future activities are lawful.
3. `[IF director ID verification]` Arrange identity verification of the company's directors and PSCs for Companies House through Tax Assessments and Compliance Services (TACS), as Companies House requires under the Economic Crime and Corporate Transparency Act 2023.
4. `[IF included]` File simple changes during the year (change of registered office, appointment or resignation of an officer) at the fee in your quote.

**Fee basis:** our fee includes the Companies House filing fee for the confirmation statement.

**You agree to:** tell us promptly about any change to officers, shareholders, PSCs, addresses or share capital; confirm the details are correct before we file; and keep the company's registered email address up to date. **The directors remain legally responsible for the company's filings being accurate and on time.**

D7.title: Payroll (RTI) and pensions auto-enrolment
D7.body:
**We will, for each pay period ({{payroll_frequency}}):**

1. Calculate gross to net pay for each employee and director, including PAYE (including Scottish and Welsh rates), employee and employer National Insurance, student and postgraduate loan deductions, statutory payments (sick, maternity, paternity and others) and their recovery, and the Employment Allowance claim where eligible.
2. Calculate workplace pension contributions for employees in your pension scheme, from the information you give us.
3. Send you payslips (or publish them through payroll software), a payroll summary, and a report of PAYE, NIC and pension amounts due with their payment dates.
4. Submit the Full Payment Submission (FPS) to HMRC on or before each payday, after you approve it (or on the basis of the data you provided), and an Employer Payment Summary (EPS) by the 19th of the following month where needed.
5. At the tax year end, submit the final FPS or EPS, and prepare P60s for you to give employees by 31 May. Prepare P45s for leavers.
6. `[IF auto-enrolment]` Assess each worker's auto-enrolment category each pay period, deduct and report contributions to your pension provider, and help you with the declaration of compliance to The Pensions Regulator and re-enrolment every 3 years.
7. Deal only with your nominated person. We will refer questions from individual employees back to you.

**Fee basis:** your fee covers the number of employees in your quote. If the number rises, we will tell you and agree the new fee.

**Not included:** setting up the PAYE scheme (Schedule D9), P11D benefits returns, IR35 and off-payroll status advice, termination payment advice, choosing a pension scheme (we are not authorised to give pension advice), paying employees or HMRC, and correcting earlier years.

**You agree to:** tell us about new starters (full name, address, date of birth, NI number, starter checklist), leavers, pay changes, hours, absences, bonuses and pension changes at least 3 working days before each payday; approve payroll before submission; pay employees, HMRC and the pension provider on time; choose and keep a qualifying pension scheme, write to workers about auto-enrolment within the legal time limits, and handle opt-in and opt-out requests; and keep payroll records for at least 3 years after the tax year (6 years for pension records). **As the employer you are legally responsible for the payroll data and submissions being correct and on time, and for paying tax, NIC and pensions on time.** If information is late, we will try to meet the payday but are not liable for penalties caused by the delay.

**Data-processing annex (UK GDPR Article 28) — forms part of Schedule D7**

- **Subject matter and purpose:** running your payroll and auto-enrolment, and making submissions to HMRC and your pension provider.
- **Duration:** for the length of this engagement, plus the retention period below.
- **Personal data:** names, addresses, dates of birth, NI numbers, tax codes, pay, hours, bank details, absence and statutory payment details (which may include health information, such as fit notes), pension and student loan details.
- **Data subjects:** your employees, directors and workers.
- **Our duties as your processor:** we will (a) process the data only on your documented instructions, unless the law requires otherwise, in which case we will tell you unless the law forbids it; (b) ensure anyone processing it is bound by confidentiality; (c) keep it secure with appropriate technical and organisational measures (encrypted cloud storage, multi-factor authentication, password-protected or portal-only file transfer, restricted access); (d) use sub-processors only with your consent, which you give by accepting this schedule for our payroll software and cloud providers listed in our privacy notice, and on the same data protection terms; (e) help you respond to employees exercising their data rights and with your security, breach-notification and impact-assessment duties; (f) tell you without undue delay of any personal data breach; (g) at the end of the engagement, return the data to you and then delete our copies after 6 years, except where the law requires us to keep them; (h) give you the information you need to show compliance, and allow reasonable audits; and (i) tell you immediately if we think an instruction breaks data protection law.
- **Your duties as controller:** to have a lawful basis for the processing, to give your employees a privacy notice explaining that their data is processed by your payroll provider, and to give us only the data we need.
- Nothing in this annex removes our own direct responsibilities under UK GDPR.

D8.title: VAT returns (Making Tax Digital for VAT)
D8.body:
**We will:**

1. Prepare your VAT returns for each VAT period from your digital records and the information you give us, using the VAT scheme you are registered for (standard, cash accounting, flat rate or annual accounting).
2. Submit each return through MTD-compatible software after you approve it, by the deadline (normally 1 month and 7 days after the period end).
3. Tell you how much VAT to pay or reclaim and when.
4. Point out errors we find in earlier returns and how they can be corrected.

**Not included:** VAT registration or deregistration (Schedule D9), advice on partial exemption, the Capital Goods Scheme, international or property VAT, VAT inspections, and error correction or voluntary disclosures beyond simple adjustments.

**You agree to:** keep digital records that meet MTD for VAT rules; give us full records for the period within 10 days after it ends (we need at least 5 working days before the deadline); keep valid VAT invoices for purchases you reclaim; pay the VAT by the deadline; and tell us about errors you find later so we can help correct them. **You are legally responsible for your VAT returns being correct and filed and paid on time.** Late returns and payments attract HMRC penalty points, penalties and interest.

D9.title: Registrations and one-off services
D9.body:
Each item below is a one-off service. The engagement for that item ends when the work is completed.

| Service | We will | You agree to |
|---|---|---|
| Self Assessment registration | Register you for Self Assessment (and Class 2/4 NIC where relevant) so HMRC issues your UTR. Register by 5 October after the end of the tax year you started. | Give us your full name, address, NI number, date of birth, business start date and details. Forward HMRC's letters with your UTR to us. |
| VAT registration | Prepare and submit your VAT registration, and advise on the effective date and the most suitable VAT scheme from the information you give. | Tell us as soon as your turnover may exceed £90,000 in any rolling 12 months. You must register within 30 days of the end of the month in which you exceed it. Late registration penalties are not our responsibility if you told us late. |
| PAYE (payroll) registration | Register you as an employer with HMRC and set up the PAYE scheme in our payroll software. | Give us the details HMRC requires, including the first payday. You must register before the first payday. |
| Workplace pension setup (auto-enrolment) | Work out your auto-enrolment duties start date, set up the pension scheme you have chosen in our payroll software, help you write to your workers, and complete your declaration of compliance with The Pensions Regulator within 5 months of your duties start date. | Choose and open a qualifying pension scheme (we are not authorised to advise on which), give us the provider's details, and pay contributions on time. You remain legally responsible for your auto-enrolment duties. |
| MTD for Income Tax sign-up or setup package | Sign you up for MTD for Income Tax and set up and connect your software, as described in your quote. Includes the authority in Schedule D2. | Confirm the information is correct and that you understand sign-up generally cannot be reversed by choice. |
| One-off MTD quarterly update or year-end submission | Prepare and submit the single update or final declaration named in your quote, as described in Schedule D2. | Provide complete digital records for that period. |
| Employment expenses claim (P87) | Prepare and submit a claim for tax relief on employment expenses you paid and were not reimbursed, for the tax years in your quote (up to 4 years back). | Confirm each expense was paid by you, used wholly for your job, and not repaid by your employer. Keep receipts. Claims over £2,500 a year must be made through a Self Assessment return (Schedule D1). |
| Catch-up work | Bring your records or overdue returns up to date for the periods listed in your quote, on the same terms as the matching schedule above. | Provide all missing records. If records are incomplete, we will tell you and agree how any estimates are made. |
